objective: Evaluate the effectiveness of the Nucleus invention in reducing bacterial colonization rate on Dacron grafts
independent_variables: Presence of antimicrobial nanofibers on Dacron grafts
dependent_variables: Bacterial colonization rate on the graft surface after 7 days of implantation
controls: Current Dacron graft with no antimicrobial treatment
baseline: Current Dacron graft with no antimicrobial treatment
procedure: Prepare Dacron grafts with and without antimicrobial nanofibers
Inoculate the grafts with Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli bacteria in a 1:1 ratio to nanofibers
Implant the grafts in a controlled in vitro environment for 7 days
Assess the bacterial colonization rate on the graft surface
expected_result: A 45% reduction in bacterial colonization rate on grafts with antimicrobial nanofibers compared to the baseline
falsification_condition: No significant reduction in bacterial colonization rate (p-value > 0.05) or an increase in colonization rate compared to the baseline
sample_requirements: At least 30 Dacron grafts with and without antimicrobial nanofibers, and 30 grafts with non-antimicrobial nanofibers
safety_constraints: Ensure proper handling and disposal of biological samples, and follow standard laboratory safety protocols
information_gain: Understanding the effectiveness of the Nucleus invention in reducing bacterial colonization rate on Dacron grafts, and identifying potential areas for improvement
